central_unknown: Ferrari brought major upgrades and topped both Friday sessions, but historically they have flattered on Fridays before fading. The key uncertainty is whether Ferrari's upgrade gains are real and sustainable into qualifying/race, and whether Mercedes or Red Bull emerge as the stronger second constructor.

budget_tiers.core: Verstappen or Antonelli (captain), Leclerc, Ferrari constructor
budget_tiers.fills: Hulkenberg, Bearman, one Racing Bulls driver (Lawson or Lindblad)
Hulkenberg, Bearman, Bortoleto (differential gamble from back of grid)

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: FanAmp has Verstappen as a lock for 2x captain, finishing P2 and P3 in both Friday sessions. ML projects VER at 28.8 exp pts, ppm 1.6, MEDIUM risk for Mexico (nearest ML data available), consistently the top projected driver. However, Hadjar's struggles with the car ('horrendous' per Isaac) slightly weaken Red Bull constructor appeal.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Finished P2 in FP2 and has been a consistent top-tier captain option all season. ML projects ANT at 28.4 exp pts, ppm 1.19, LOW risk — very close to Verstappen. FanAmp says Antonelli could usurp Verstappen for 2x if Mercedes show more pace in FP3. Mercedes pit stop form also favors this pick.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: Topped both FP1 and FP2 with Ferrari's big upgrade package. Leclerc himself said one big package can vault a constructor from P4 to P1. ML projects LEC at 24.9 exp pts, ppm 1.76, MEDIUM risk — best value among top drivers. Channels unanimously rate him as a lock. Risk: Ferrari have historically flattered on Fridays.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Six consecutive 0.6M price increases. 81% chance of another price rise per F1 Fantasy Tools. FP1 power unit concerns resolved after setup change in FP2. Budget anchor.

buy.name: Oliver Bearman
buy.note: Good overtaking in Singapore. -7 points for price rise, 82% chance per F1 Fantasy Tools. Solid budget option to round out the team.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: FanAmp and PolePosition both favor Lawson slightly over Lindblad long-term. Strong Singapore result (17 pts). Saves 0.1M vs Lindblad. 82% chance of max price rise. Lawson himself noted COTA Turn 1 chaos can create huge gains for midfielders.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: 5-place grid penalty for new ICE gives overtake opportunities. FanAmp rates him equally with Lawson — a trade-off between Lindblad's positions-gained upside vs Lawson's better price target. 59% chance of max price rise.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: High-risk, high-reward differential. 20-place grid penalty puts him at the back — could gain 15-20 points via overtakes. But almost certain 0.6M price drop. Only for teams with 140M+ budget who can absorb the loss.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: Scored 12 points in two consecutive races. 60% chance of price rise per F1 Fantasy Tools. PolePosition rates him underrated but prefers Lawson/Lindblad at similar price.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: PolePosition flagged him as a one-week budget option at 60% price rise chance. COTA is not his ideal track type though — more power-dependent than Singapore/Malaysia. FanAmp noted Aston Martin struggled in both sessions.

avoid: Alex Albon — did not complete a representative lap in either session due to track limits; Williams struggling badly
Franco Colapinto — 10-place grid penalty, DNF'd sprint and race in Singapore, needs 39 points to avoid price drop
Williams constructor — complained throughout both sessions, worst Friday performance on the grid
Sergio Perez — transfer trap per PolePosition; inconsistent results with untimely DNFs despite low price

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: PolePosition notes this is the start of a triple-header with only 6 races left in the season. If your team needs significant restructuring (e.g., getting Lawson in, pivoting constructors from Red Bull to Ferrari), using it now sets up the run-in. Otherwise save for Mexico or São Paulo.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: No sprint weekend reduces total scoring potential. Channels suggest saving 3x for a sprint weekend where the multiplier applies across more scoring events. However, if Ferrari's upgrades are confirmed strong and you have Leclerc as captain, it could be tempting.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: BoxBox analysis from Monza showed limitless can sometimes score less than a well-constructed 3x team. Save for a sprint weekend or a round with clearer constructor dominance.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Keep in reserve for the triple-header. Could be useful at Mexico or São Paulo if a late injury/penalty emerges.

watch_items: FP3 performance of Ferrari — confirm whether Friday pace is genuine or a repeat of past false dawns
Isack Hadjar's feedback on the Red Bull car — if still struggling, pivot constructor from Red Bull to Mercedes
George Russell's FP3 pace on representative tires — ran mediums in FP2 making true pace unclear
Turn 1 carnage risk at COTA — Lawson called it 'a lottery'; 2025 sprint saw Norris, Piastri, Hulkenberg, Alonso all taken out
McLaren upgrade integration — Norris says big packages take time, may not click immediately this weekend
Track limits enforcement in qualifying — Albon already hit in both sessions; could affect others
Hulkenberg power unit situation — resolved in FP2 but monitor FP3 for any recurrence
arc: The United States GP kicks off the Americas triple-header (COTA → Mexico → São Paulo). Ferrari's big upgrade makes this a pivotal weekend for constructor valuation — if the gains hold, Ferrari becomes a must-own through Mexico and Brazil. The COTA result will also clarify whether McLaren's upgrade needs time to bed in, which could make them a buy-low for Mexico. Budget drivers like Hulkenberg and Lawson are in prime position for continued price rises across the triple-header, making them essential holds. Save aggressive chips for sprint weekends later in the run-in, but consider a Wildcard now if your team structure needs a reset before the final six races.
